key_insight: Aligning white blood cell images with karyotype and mutation data creates stronger patient representations for hematological diagnosis.
clinical_relevance: This approach could better support blood cancer diagnosis workflows by combining visual cytology with genetic information, improving retrieval of diseases and genetic alterations.
method: Stage 1: self-supervised vision-only pretraining of a transformer aggregator with an iBOT head on 1500+ patients.
Stage 2: supervised contrastive genetic alignment using acute myeloid leukemia patients.
Learned patient embeddings were evaluated on diagnostic tasks and retrieval of genetic alterations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved hematological diagnostic performance, outperforming slide-level histopathology foundation models, with training on over 1500 patients.
watch_item: The method depends on paired genetic data and may be harder to deploy in settings where karyotype or targeted mutation panels are not routinely available.
paper_title: Genetically Aligned Patient Representations Improve Hematological Diagnosis
